abstract: Audio deepfake detection (ADD) aims to distinguish bonafide speech from synthetic or manipulated speech. Representations from different layers of self-supervised learning (SSL) speech encoders vary in their ability to distinguish bonafide from spoofed speech. Comparing representations of the same utterance across encoder depths may reveal useful spoofing cues, yet common layer-selection and aggregation methods do not provide these comparisons as detection inputs. We propose Cross-Layer Relation Modeling (\ours{}), which explicitly encodes cross-layer relations alongside layer-specific features, making both directly available for ADD. CLRM reuses the existing detector's SSL encoder and identifies informative layer pairs by combining speaker-relative representation geometry with source-domain detection performance. The resulting relation score is fused with the detector's original score, requiring only the training of compact relation heads and fusion parameters while keeping the existing detector frozen. Across five external datasets, CLRM reduces the mean equal error rate (EER) for all three evaluated detectors, achieving relative reductions of 7.8--16.7%. Controlled comparisons with identical layer summaries and approximately matched auxiliary-head parameter counts also show a lower mean EER for explicit relations than direct concatenation, both before and after score fusion. These findings support explicit cross-layer comparisons as useful detection inputs for SSL-based audio deepfake detectors.
oneSentenceThesis: 针对跨合成方法和跨录音条件的音频伪造检测，CLRM 复用冻结检测器的 XLS-R 编码器，对选定的两个层做显式跨层比较并与原分数融合，在五个外部数据集上把三类检测器的平均等错误率相对降低 7.8%–16.7%，代价是只训练紧凑的关系头和融合参数。
originalTitle: CLRM: Cross-Layer Relation Modeling for Audio Deepfake Detection
readerTitle: CLRM：把同一句话在编码器不同深度的表示拿来直接比较
